raw_response:
I'm 55 this year, been farming these 20 mu for 30 years now. Never went to school, can't read those chemical labels, but I know my land. It's me and my old man, just the two of us. We got the south 10 mu where we grow cabbage — three crops a year, been doing that for 15 years since the vegetable dealer started coming to the village. The north 10 mu is our wheat and corn, can't stop that, we need the grain for flour and feed.

The wheat is already in the ground from last October. Right now it's sleeping. Come March, when it turns green, I'll spread the spring fertilizer — about 20 jin of urea per mu, I just know it as a bit less than half a small bag. I irrigate twice more before harvest in early June. The combine comes, costs 50 yuan per mu. Last year we got about 900 jin per mu, hoping for the same this year if the spring rain cooperates.

For the spring cabbage, I already started the seedlings in the little plot behind the house in February. Early April, I'll transplant about 4 mu. I hire six or seven women from the village — 80 yuan a day now, everything's gone up. I put down two big bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, plus two cartloads of chicken manure. The manure is free from our chickens, but the compound is 150 yuan a bag. When the heads start wrapping tight, I topdress with another half bag of urea. I water five times. The bugs are bad in spring — I spray four times for cabbage worms and that downy mildew. Hope to get 9000 jin per mu.

After we cut the spring cabbage in mid-June, we got maybe ten days to turn the field. We put in the summer cabbage — about 3 mu worth this time because the heat makes it risky and I don't want to lose everything if a heat wave hits. Same compound fertilizer but less manure, no time to haul it all. Water six times, spray five times for bugs. Yield might only be 8000 jin per mu but summer prices are usually better, so it evens out.

Then early September, we put in the autumn cabbage on the rest — 3 mu. Autumn is the best, fewer bugs, big heads. I put manure down again since I have a bit more time. Four waters, three sprays. Should get 10,000 jin per mu, and prices are good before winter when everyone wants cabbage.

For the corn, it goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. I use the corn planter — one big bag of compound per mu at planting. If it looks yellow later, maybe I spread a bit of urea, but usually not. Two waters, one spray for armyworm. Machine harvest in late September. Should get about 1000 jin per mu.

Money is tight this year. Fertilizer went up again at the dealer. I need to keep my total spending around 22,000 yuan. The cabbage makes the real money but eats up the most cash. I'm spending more on cabbage fertilizer because if I under-do it and the yield drops, I lose big — last year my neighbor tried to save on fertilizer and her spring cabbage was half the size. For wheat and corn, I keep it simple — they don't pay as well per mu. I need to keep 5,000 yuan aside for hiring labor, can't do all that cabbage transplanting and cutting ourselves. And I always keep some cash in the house for emergencies.
